{{Short description|Theoretical bound used in estimation theory}}
The '''Ziv–Zakai bound''' (named after [[Jacob Ziv]] and [[Moshe Zakai]]<ref name="ziv-zakai-1969">{{cite journal
 |last1=Ziv
 |first1=J.
 |last2=Zakai
 |first2=M.
 |title=Some lower bounds on signal parameter estimation
 |journal=[[IEEE Transactions on Information Theory]]
 |volume=15
 |issue=3
 |pages=386–391
 |year=1969
|doi=10.1109/TIT.1969.1054301
 }}</ref>) is used in [[estimation theory|theory of estimations]] to provide a [[lower bound]] on possible-probable error involving some random parameter <math> X </math> from a [[Noise|noisy]] observation <math> Y </math>. The bound works by connecting probability of the excess error to the [[hypothesis testing]]. The bound is considered to be tighter than [[Cramér–Rao bound]] albeit more involved.  Several modern versions of the bound have been introduced <ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Bell
 |first1=K.
 |last2=Steinberg
 |first2=Y.
 |last3=Ephraim
 |first3=Y.
 |last4=Van Trees
 |first4=H.
 |title=Extended Ziv–Zakai lower bound for vector parameter estimation
 |journal=[[IEEE Transactions on Information Theory]]
 |volume=43
 |issue=2
 |pages=624–637
 |year=1997
|doi=10.1109/18.556118
 }}</ref> following the original version published in 1969.<ref name="ziv-zakai-1969"/>

== Simple Form of the Bound ==
Suppose we want to estimate a random variable <math>X</math> with the [[probability density]] <math> f_X </math> from a noisy observation <math> Y </math>. Then for  any estimator <math>g</math> a simple form of Ziv-Zakai bound is given by<ref name="ziv-zakai-1969" />

<math>
\begin{aligned}
& \mathbb{E}\bigl[|X - g(Y)|^2\bigr] \ge \frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\infty} t
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \bigl(f_X(x) + f_X(x+t)\bigr)\, P_e(x, x+t)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t,
\end{aligned}
</math>

where 
<math>P_e(x, x+t)</math> is the minimum (Bayes) error probability for the binary hypothesis testing problem between

<math>
\begin{aligned} 
 \mathcal{H}_0&: Y \mid X = x \\
\mathcal{H}_1&:  Y \mid X = x + t
\end{aligned}
</math>

with prior probabilities 
<math>\Pr(\mathcal{H}_0) = \frac{f_X(x)}{f_X(x) + f_X(x + t) }</math> 
and 
<math>\Pr(\mathcal{H}_1) = 1 - \Pr(\mathcal{H}_0)</math>.

== Generalization ==
The original lower bound can be tightened by introducing a notion of the valley-filling function, which for a function <math>f</math> 

<math>
\mathcal{V}_t(f) = \sup_{u: u \ge t} f(u)
</math>

with the bound given by 

<math>
\begin{aligned}
& \mathbb{E}\bigl[|X - g(Y)|^2\bigr] \ge \frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\infty} t
\mathcal{V} \left\{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \bigl(f_X(x) + f_X(x+t)\bigr)\, P_e(x, x+t)\,\mathrm{d}x\, \right\}\mathrm{d}t,
\end{aligned}
</math>

The most general version of the bound, which holds for both continuous and discrete random vectors, is also available.<ref name="Jeong2025">{{cite journal
 |last1=Jeong
 |first1=M.
 |last2=Dytso
 |first2=A.
 |last3=Cardone
 |first3=M.
 |title=A Comprehensive Study on Ziv-Zakai Lower Bounds on the MMSE
 |journal=[[IEEE Transactions on Information Theory]]
 |volume=71
 |issue=4
 |pages=3214–3236
 |year=2025
 |doi=10.1109/TIT.2025.3541987
 |publisher=[[IEEE]]
}}</ref> 

== Tightness ==
Ziv-Zakai bound has some general tightness guarantees, such as<ref name="Jeong2025" />

* For continuous random variables:
** The bound is tight in the high signal-to-noise ratio regime for continuous random vectors.
** In the low signal-to-noise ratio regime, the bound is tight if unimodal and symmetric with respect to its mode.
* For discrete random variables:
** The bound requires a valley-filling function; otherwise, the bound is equal to zero.
** The bound is typically not tight for discrete random variables. 
** A version of the bound known as the single point Ziv-Zakai bound is generally tighter than other versions of Ziv-Zakai. 


== Applications ==
The Ziv-Zakai bound has several appealing advantages. Unlike the
other bounds, the Ziv-Zakai bound  only requires one regularity
condition, that is, the parameter under estimation needs to
have a probability density function. Hence, the Ziv-Zakai bound  has a broader
applicability than, for instance, the [[Cramér-Rao bound]], which
requires several smoothness assumptions on the probability density function of the
estimand.

Some of the use-cases that have been informed by the Ziv-Zakai bound are:
